purpose: Source-critical person-predicate and 1975/1977 Momostenango ethnographic day-count checks; separate contemporary Zunil, historical Lowland codices, and Central Mexican Borgia contexts.

source_books.author: Barbara Tedlock
source_books.title: Time and the Highland Maya
source_books.edition: revised 1992, University of New Mexico Press
source_books.cultural_scope: Momostenango K'iche' fieldwork with other highland comparisons

source_books.editors: Gabrielle Vail and Anthony F. Aveni
source_books.title: The Madrid Codex: New Approaches to Understanding an Ancient Maya Manuscript
source_books.edition: 2004 University Press of Colorado; owned PDF scans first paperback 2009
source_books.cultural_scope: Madrid codex Lowland Maya calendrics; comparative Borgia Central Mexican material separated

dated_ethnographic_day_witnesses.source_context: Author states her elicitation on this exact date began with current day; independently dated local label rather than later chart reconstruction.
Author dates entry of Mam 4 Ik at a shrine, not a modern birth sign.
Author dates entry of Secretary 4 Tziquin; exactly 13 civil days after the 4 Ik Mam entry.

ethnographic_cross_validation.reference_lowland_independent_source: Smithsonian NMAI Living Maya Time, 2012-12-21=4 Ajaw and 2012-12-20=3 Kawak; source anchor separately documented in preexisting test_maya_calendar_reference.py
ethnographic_cross_validation.result_scope: Documented arithmetic parity of a selected Lowland correlation with Tedlock's dated Momostenango field reports in 1975-77 only; NOT full proof of every region, era, birth clock policy, or natal traits.

source_critical_findings.paraphrase: The ethnographer explicitly challenges assigning a single universal start day to the continuous 260-day count. Momostenango informants did not consistently name an initial day.
source_critical_findings.contrast: Zunil Komon Tohil daykeepers describe B'atz' renewal/new year ceremony; ritual renewal does not necessarily claim a mathematically privileged epoch.

source_critical_findings.paraphrase: Numbers affect specific rites, shrines and interpreted strength; lower 1-3, middle 7-9, upper 11-13 differ in ethnographic contexts.
source_critical_findings.restriction: No arbitrary inherited 13-tone modifier applied to the Zunil natal E claim.

source_critical_findings.paraphrase: Momostenango birth-day passage associates Noj with creative, innovative thought and problem solving; separately discusses daykeeping/leadership roles.
Momostenango E birth passage discusses culturally gendered priest-shaman/midwife roles and life fortune; it does not independently predict general elective travel propensity.
Zunil daykeepers associate those born on E with being good travelers, sociable and generous.
source_critical_findings.restriction: 'good travelers' could mean ability, frequency, enjoyment or favorable journey outcome; select one before seeing responses.

source_critical_findings.paraphrase: Chapter 5 distinguishes 260-day tzolk'in ritual divination, 365-day haab', 52-year Calendar Round, and dated historical Long Count.
Chapter 8 argues that some Madrid almanacs organize annual/52-year rites rather than a 260-day-only periodicity; yearbearer pages M.34-M.37 and M.90a-M.92a are examples.
Pohl's comparative chapter discusses prognostic marriage calculation in Borgia 58-60 and ethnographic implements of Nahua/Mixtec groups. This is NOT an interpretation of a Madrid Maya natal rule.

A ceremonial day may begin at dawn, a particular solar yearbearer arrives at midnight, and uncertain dream timing can involve both adjacent days. These distinct functions do not establish a unique natal-day birth-time cutoff.

prospective_test_candidate.source_anchored_region: Momostenango K'iche', Tedlock revised 1992 printed p122
prospective_test_candidate.number_1_13_policy: pooled until birth-number modifier independently source-specified and prespecified
prospective_test_candidate.direction: higher preregistered blind-scored novel problem-solving performance than non-Noj births
prospective_test_candidate.measured_task_draft: Timed identical divergent-thinking prompts; independent masked raters grade non-redundant, applicable novelty with a fixed rubric. Specify language, age accommodations, prompts, reliability and scoring before freeze.
prospective_test_candidate.visible_to_participants_before_response: No birth sign, hypothesis, group label or expected direction
prospective_test_candidate.proposed_primary_comparison: Noj sign versus all other day names, unadjusted and predeclared demographic-adjusted (age, education, language); no outcome-guided decoy selection.
prospective_test_candidate.controls: A preregistered +1 or +2 civil-day phase shift, permuted sign labels with same birth-season structure, matched non-astrology baseline, and multiple-testing correction if testing other signs/traditions.
prospective_test_candidate.null_contrary: No positive effect on the fixed score, or outcomes better explained by non-astrology controls, must be reported as misses.
prospective_test_candidate.domain_ambiguity: A brief task measures one aspect of creativity, not all lifetime creative behavior; exact source-to-measure transfer requires independent blind content review.
prospective_test_candidate.birth_date_time_policy: Civil date and time/place recorded privately; GMT584283 is a documented Momostenango date-only development alignment, NOT validated full regional/era natal assignment; until boundary known, restrict or abstain near ambiguous day transitions.
prospective_test_candidate.cohort_policy: Consenting adults with sources independently collected, source-related local cultural cohort separately from other populations; known owner/friend survey respondents excluded from untouched validation.
prospective_test_candidate.quantitative_freeze_status: NOT_FROZEN; no sample size/power, task rubric, birth-boundary rule, calibrated effect prior, final decoys or independent review yet

Decoy/null model, family-wise test policy, enrollment and target power locked
Prediction/engine/questionnaire SHA frozen BEFORE genuine untouched participants
